C0.quote: a randomized voting rule takes as input a profile of agent preferences
C0.note: Main object is randomized voting rules, plus one- and two-sided matching mechanisms. Voting is a core part, so coded eligible.

C1.quote: We study the compatibility of efficiency and strategyproofness for randomized voting rules
C1.note: Mostly axiomatic compatibility results on efficiency, strategyproofness, fairness and stability. Algorithmic results: Theorem 10, 26. Strategyproofness is a property studied throughout.

C2.1.quote: A voting profile ≻= (≻1 , ..., ≻n ) consists of the preference ≻i of each agent

C2.2.quote: ≻i is a strict ordering over the alternatives
C2.2.note: Quantile parameter is also part of the agent's data, but the ranking is the submitted input.

C2.3.quote: Consider an agent equipped with a strict preference order ≻ among the options
C2.3.note: Agents have preferences and quantile parameters.

C2.4.quote: A voting profile ≻= (≻1 , ..., ≻n ) consists of the preference ≻i of each agent
C2.4.note: The profile of preferences is the rule's input. Rankings are called 'submitted as votes' in the introduction. Misreports appear only in strategyproofness definitions, with no explicit statement on the relation between input and held attitude.

C3.1.quote: it holds rep(R(≻), ≻i , hi ) ⪰i rep(R(≻−i , ≻′i ), ≻i , hi )
C3.1.note: Strategyproofness analyses consider misreports. Efficiency, welfare and proportionality analyses take the profile as given.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held preferences in the non-strategic analyses.

C4.1.note: Utility is defined from the ranking via quantile representatives. This is a defined link but is in effect the held-attitude model itself. The paper does use utility for ranking inputs, so the applicability condition may hold. It is coded SPEC below as the safer reading.

C5.1.quote: Given a voting instance (N, A, ≻, h), a lottery x over the alternatives of A is efficient
C5.1.note: Pareto efficiency is a main criterion. Also social welfare variant (Theorem 10) and proportionality/envy-freeness.

C5.2.quote: rep(y, ≻i , hi ) ⪰i rep(x, ≻i , hi ) for every agent i
C5.2.note: Evaluation is by the quantile utility of agents based on preferences and quantile parameters, treated as held attitudes. Not explicitly separated from the submitted input, so it could be read as INPUT-UNSTATED.

VOT.quote_behav: for every preference profile ≻, agent i, and preference ≻′i
VOT.note: Voters misreport in strategyproofness definitions. Information is not specified, since strategyproofness is a dominance-type condition.

C8.1.quote: the voting rule R is strategyproof for the domain (N, A, ·, h)

claims.quote: Randomized mechanisms are pivotal in social choice and matching theory
In contrast to well-known impossibilities in randomized social choice, we show that satisfying the above properties simultaneously is possible.
trivial mechanisms like uniform lotteries are usually ideal

C9.1.note: Claims about which rules are good and about the practical use of randomized mechanisms.

C9.2.note: Possibility claims need the assumptions that agents have quantile utilities and that submitted rankings relate to held preferences; the latter is not stated. Real-world quantile parameters are also not discussed.
